extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, area chairs, and researchers interested in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes randomized experiments run with ICML 2020 to evaluate resubmission-bias, herding in reviewer discussions, and novice reviewer recruiting, and reports measurable outcomes and policy implications for conference peer-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall evaluation (10-point Likert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' overall evaluation of a paper measured on a 10-point Likert item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key finding: reviewers give almost one point lower score (95% CI: [0.24, 1.30]) when told the paper is a resubmission. Used as primary outcome to detect resubmission bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Quality (narrow review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the narrower review criteria; reviewers tend to underrate 'Paper Quality' the most when informed a paper is a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitored as a component of reviews to see which specific evaluation dimensions are most affected by disclosure of prior rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission bias (effect of disclosure of prior rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers are biased (harsher) when they know the paper was previously rejected from a similar venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: conference organizers should trade off reduced submissions vs. unfairness; mitigation suggested: postpone revealing resubmission signal until after initial reviews are submitted. Also consider the impact of making rejected-paper reviews publicly available (e.g., on openreview.net).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of resubmission signal disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When to reveal that a submission is a resubmission (e.g., before or after initial reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation from experiment: postponing the resubmission signal until after initial reviews are submitted can reduce bias; conference policy should consider this timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of past reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether making reviews of rejected papers publicly available (on platforms like openreview.net) could introduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding: disclosure of resubmission history can bias reviewers, so publicity of past reviews must be accounted for in policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Herding in discussions (order effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the final decision depends on the order in which reviewers join the discussion (i.e., social influence/herding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment: randomized assignment to have most-positive or most-negative reviewer start discussion. Key finding: no statistically significant difference in acceptance rates between groups — no evidence of herding in discussion phase; thus no special countermeasures may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion management strategy (positive-first vs negative-first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational strategies for managing reviewer discussions: ask most-positive reviewer to start first (Positive Group) versus ask most-negative to start first (Negative Group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the experimental manipulation to test herding; the only intended difference is order of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate (as outcome metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of papers accepted — used as the main outcome to detect effects of discussion-order interventions (herding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The herding experiment analyzed ~1,500 papers and compared acceptance rates across randomized groups; no significant differences found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novice reviewer selection (experimental recruitment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting promising very-junior reviewers from an auxiliary review process (52 invited from 134 junior reviewers based on review quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: evaluate reviews in an auxiliary process and invite top performers into the conference reviewer pool; used to expand reviewer pool beyond conventional recruiting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring of novice reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing experimental reviewers with a senior researcher as a point of contact who offers additional mentoring during the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the twofold approach (selection + mentoring). Found to help produce reviews that are at least comparable and on some metrics higher-rated than the main pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality as rated by area chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Area chairs' ratings of review quality (including metric 'exceeded expectations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key finding: 30% of reviews by experimental novice reviewers exceeded expectations vs. 14% for the main pool. Used to evaluate whether recruiting novices compromises review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer pool sustainability (enlarging without compromising quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to increase the number of available reviewers to handle submission growth while maintaining review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment shows selection + mentoring can bring strong reviewers from less-conventional populations; recommended to replicate at larger scale and evaluate components separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of auxiliary review processes to evaluate reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Run a separate/auxiliary review process to generate reviews from candidate junior reviewers and use those reviews to select experimental reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary process also provided useful reviews to participating authors who were not submitting to a real conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design standards (randomized controlled trials, sample sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and sufficiently large samples (e.g., ~1,500 papers, ~2,000 reviewers) to test interventions in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post emphasizes RCT methodology for causal inference in peer-review experiments and reports confidence intervals and significance testing (e.g., 95% CI for resubmission effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting (confidence intervals and significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report point estimates with confidence intervals and test for statistical significance when evaluating interventions (e.g., 95% CI for score differences; tests of acceptance-rate differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify uncertainty (resubmission effect CI given) and to conclude absence/presence of effects (no significant difference in herding experiment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy trade-off evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate trade-offs between intended benefits of policies (e.g., reducing reviewer load by discouraging resubmissions) and unintended harms (e.g., introducing bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers must weigh benefits vs potential unfairness; experiments inform whether to adopt or modify policies (e.g., resubmission-declaration rules).
